question: What is the native app descriptor layout and the register/unregister ABI? (CAN-APP-002/003)
prototype_hypothesis: app_launcher_add(const launcher_app_descriptor *d) -> int; app_launcher_del(u16 appid) -> int. Descriptor: name@+8, icon@+12 (required), app_id u16@+16, flags@+18 (bit2 uninstallable), icon_resolver fn@+28, hidden@+60 bit0.
callsite_evidence: app_launcher_add = sub_C4F2BDC: load_app_info(sub_C4F2898) -> record; searches runtime list 0x200D090C by name (record.name @ record+8); inserts into apps table 0x200D0924; links via sub_C4F7004; logs 'add icon: %s'
load_app_info = sub_C4F2898: rejects null, missing icon (+12==0), hidden (+60&1); warns on not-uninstallable (+18&4); builds record {u16 app_id@0, icon_handle@4, name@8, icon_name@12, flags@20 bit1}
app_launcher_del = sub_C4F2CC4: log 'app_launcher_del app'; finds record in 0x200D0924 by u16 id; sub_C4F6DF8 cleanup; removes from apps table + page list; frees both (sub_C587B10)
hide (System msg 26, EVID-APP-002) calls app_launcher_del(appid); show (msg 27) rebuilds the UI
control_flow_evidence: logs 'The app has no icon to launch itself %s', 'The app need hidden %s', 'The app can't be uninstalled %s', 'App is (%s, %s)'
icon_resolver called twice: once as (a1+28)(a1, default_icon) returning display string, once as (a1+28)(a1) returning the icon handle
ownership_analysis: descriptor borrowed from the module; the launcher copies name/icon pointers into its own record and owns icon_handle (freed on del)
unsafe_assumptions: the field at descriptor+0 (reserved0, 8 bytes) is not read by load_app_info but may be a magic/size checked elsewhere
the exact call convention for the register entry (whether modules call app_launcher_add directly or through a wrapper) not yet proven
icon resource format (bitmap/png/theme ref) not yet recovered
recommended_probe: host parse of the descriptor layout; a minimal register probe with a synthetic descriptor + dummy icon resolver
